items.headline: Greed rises to 89 while Valuation remains 87
items.summary: The live AGCI engine moved to Greed 89/100, up 2 daily and 26 over seven days, while Valuation remains 87/100. Both are Extreme and the matrix remains EUPHORIA_RISK / Capital preservation / Do not chase.
items.whyItMatters: Complacency intensified further without a valuation reset; VIX and options term structure are both near the most complacent end of the model.

items.headline: Fed rhetoric reinforces higher-for-longer risk
items.summary: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said the economy may be firming and inflation is broader than energy and tariff shocks, while Boston Fed President Susan Collins also backed the recent hike and highlighted elevated inflation risks. The dollar reached a two-month high as markets leaned further toward restrictive policy.
items.whyItMatters: The post-hike message reduces the case for aggressively extending duration and raises the hurdle rate for long-duration equities and real estate.

items.headline: Crude supply improves but diesel stress remains extreme
items.summary: Oil held near two-week lows as Saudi crude flows improved after the East-West restart and diplomacy remained in focus, but diesel cracks reached record levels and regional shipping remains impaired.
items.whyItMatters: Lower crude reduces the headline inflation tail risk, but record refining stress means transport and goods inflation can remain sticky even if Brent falls.

items.headline: Meta Muse creates revenue optionality and new agentic-AI risks
items.summary: Wall Street is treating Meta's Muse agent as a potential new revenue engine after rapid adoption, while Reuters separately reported Meta is testing a human-concierge layer and global banks are warning that AI shopping agents can increase fraud, scam and data-privacy risks.
items.whyItMatters: Consumer agentic AI is moving from engagement to transactions. The opportunity is material, but privacy, payments liability, fraud controls and human-in-the-loop economics must enter underwriting.

items.headline: Banks face AI competition as yield curve pressure persists
items.summary: U.S. financial stocks fell as investors weighed competition from AI-driven financial tools alongside a flatter yield curve. The development links technology disruption directly to bank revenue and margin expectations.
items.whyItMatters: AI is becoming a sector-rotation and margin-risk variable for financials rather than only a technology-sector catalyst.

items.headline: All Aboard the AI Hype Train / Review & Preview: Musing Over AI / Daily Roundup
items.summary: New Barron's newsletters emphasize record-setting Nasdaq momentum around Meta Muse, persistent Fed inflation concerns, diesel-policy risk for refiners and pressure on bank stocks as AI competition enters the financial-services narrative.
items.whyItMatters: The premium-news signal corroborates public evidence that AI enthusiasm is broadening at the same time macro policy remains restrictive and sector-level disruption is increasing.
